lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.unitTitle: Time, Belongings, and Asking for Help
lessonRef.title: Correction and reflection: repairing a forgotten job

standardsRefs: Manuel Academy Ready for Life elementary sequence — Grade 3
Ready for Life v1 safety, supervision, and no-shame policy reference
Manuel Academy RFL G3 Unit 5 — time, belongings, and help-seeking
Manuel Academy local Ready for Life composition
objective: I can practice repairing a forgotten job. I will do one step at a time and check one result.
scenario: The learner looks back over the last few days and names one real job that did not get done on time, does that job now in full, then chooses and tests one concrete memory cue, such as a note by the door, an item moved to a visible spot, or a small checklist taped where the job actually happens.
materials: learner-local: tape or a way to post the cue where the job happens

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g3-u05-l06-model-card. Watch one complete example.

prompts.text: Name the first move in the model and explain why it comes first.

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g3-u05-l06-guided-card. Do the coached move.

prompts.text: Name the move you completed and the success check it meets.

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g3-u05-l06-independent-card. Choose one complete route. Follow its steps.

prompts.text: Which complete route did you use?
Record the completed step numbers and one non-sensitive result statement.

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g3-u05-l06-evidence-record. Save one result and one reflection.

prompts.text: Describe the specific forgotten job and the specific memory cue you chose, and explain why that particular cue fits the place where the job happens.

remediation: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g3-u05-l06-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step. Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g3-u05-l06-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check. Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments. Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g3-u05-l06-retry-pair without the coach prompt. Exit: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Repair completion: The forgotten job is completed fully during the lesson. | Memory cue specificity: The cue is a concrete object or note placed exactly where the job happens, and it is tested at least once. | No self-blame framing: The learner describes the specific forgotten job factually, with no character or blame language. Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g3-u05-l06-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.
extension: Have the learner pick a second job that was forgotten in a different week and design a different memory cue for it, so cues stay matched to the specific job instead of one cue being reused everywhere.

productionDepth.practicalGoal: I can practice repairing a forgotten job. I will do one step at a time and check one result.

duration.elapsedWindow: Up to seven days; use only the check-ins explicitly named in the task
duration.sessionPattern: 5 minutes model, 5–7 minutes guided try, 10–15 minutes learner task, 5 minutes evidence and retry check
duration.adultTime: No adult time required unless the learner chooses support

localMaterials.label: tape or a way to post the cue where the job happens
localMaterials.availabilityRule: Use only when already available, safe, permitted, and appropriate. The complete fictional route replaces unavailable real-world access.

materials.noPurchaseRule: No purchase is required. Use the complete fictional route when a local material, setting, source, or adult is unavailable.

resources.title: repairing a forgotten job worked model
resources.purpose: Shows the starting condition, visible moves, reasoning, and success check before the learner begins.
content: Starting condition: The learner looks back over the last few days and names one real job that did not get done on time, does that job now in full, then chooses and tests one concrete memory cue, such as a note by the door, an item moved to a visible spot, or a small checklist taped where the job actually happens.
Model move 1: Read the condition and name the exact repairing a forgotten job decision or action.
Model move 2: Before fixing anything, find the exact job that was forgotten.
Model move 3: Describe the job factually, complete it fully, then design and place a memory cue where the job happens.

Model check: Repair completion: The forgotten job is completed fully during the lesson. | Memory cue specificity: The cue is a concrete object or note placed exactly where the job happens, and it is tested at least once. | No self-blame framing: The learner describes the specific forgotten job factually, with no character or blame language.

resources.title: repairing a forgotten job action steps
resources.purpose: Provides the ordered directions used by the model, guided attempt, independent task, and retry.
content: 1. Read the goal for repairing a forgotten job.
2. Watch the worked move on swk-rfl-g3-u05-l06-model-card.
3. Do one coached move on swk-rfl-g3-u05-l06-guided-card.
4. Complete the chosen route on swk-rfl-g3-u05-l06-independent-card.
5. Save the small record on swk-rfl-g3-u05-l06-evidence-record; use swk-rfl-g3-u05-l06-retry-pair if a step is missed.

resources.title: repairing a forgotten job coached first attempt
resources.purpose: Carries the complete first attempt and a fresh correction turn.
content: Fictional practice condition: The learner looks back over the last few days and names one real job that did not get done on time, does that job now in full, then chooses and tests one concrete memory cue, such as a note by the door, an item moved to a visible spot, or a small checklist taped where the job actually happens.
Coach direction: Before fixing anything, find the exact job that was forgotten.
Learner prompt: Name the one specific job or step you forgot or skipped this week.
Feedback check: name the move completed, point to the matching success check, and identify one missing or uncertain step without judging the learner.
Fresh correction turn: use the same fictional condition with one constraint changed; restate the changed constraint, redo only the affected step, and check the new result.

resources.title: repairing a forgotten job complete application
resources.purpose: Contains the lesson-specific application directions and prompts; it is the delivered card referenced by the learner flow.
content: Application direction: Describe the job factually, complete it fully, then design and place a memory cue where the job happens.
Response 1 (t2-p1): I described the forgotten job specifically and factually, not as 'I'm bad at remembering things.'
Response 2 (t2-p2): I completed the forgotten job fully today.
Response 3 (t2-p3): I chose one concrete memory cue and placed it exactly where the job happens.
Response 4 (t2-p4): I tested the memory cue at least once today to see whether I noticed it.
Equal-access rule: Use the fictional condition above and complete the same reasoning and evidence without private real-world details.

resources.title: repairing a forgotten job minimal evidence record
resources.purpose: Defines exactly what the learner saves and what must not be collected.
content: Record only: selected route, completed step numbers, one non-sensitive result statement, and one revision if a step changed.
Reflection: Describe the specific forgotten job and the specific memory cue you chose, and explain why that particular cue fits the place where the job happens.

Success checks: Repair completion: The forgotten job is completed fully during the lesson. | Memory cue specificity: The cue is a concrete object or note placed exactly where the job happens, and it is tested at least once. | No self-blame framing: The learner describes the specific forgotten job factually, with no character or blame language.
Do not collect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations; account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details; photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules.

resources.title: repairing a forgotten job supported and parallel retry cards
resources.purpose: Delivers a real correction loop rather than a direction to try again without support.
content: Contrast reteach: compare the model check on swk-rfl-g3-u05-l06-model-card with the missed or unsupported step; name the one observable difference.
Supported card: return to swk-rfl-g3-u05-l06-guided-card, complete the affected move with one coach prompt, and receive criterion-specific feedback.
Parallel card: use a fresh fictional repairing a forgotten job condition with one changed constraint; complete the same move without the coach prompt.

Exit check: the corrected move meets this lesson's checks — Repair completion: The forgotten job is completed fully during the lesson. | Memory cue specificity: The cue is a concrete object or note placed exactly where the job happens, and it is tested at least once. | No self-blame framing: The learner describes the specific forgotten job factually, with no character or blame language..
Return: resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g3-u05-l06-independent-card; a physical route resumes only when the authorized adult says it is safe.

simulationRoute.title: repairing a forgotten job — complete fictional route
simulationRoute.directions: Complete the repairing a forgotten job task using the fictional condition and invented, non-sensitive details on the delivered independent card.
simulationRoute.completionCondition: Complete the same decision, procedure, evidence, and revision checks as the real-life route. No adult attests that a physical event occurred.

independentTask.privacyAlternative: The learner may use invented names, dates, amounts, organizations, spaces, and circumstances whenever real details are unnecessary or private.

retry.trigger: Start the correction loop when a required step is missing, the reason does not match the condition, a safety or privacy boundary is crossed, or the evidence does not show the stated result.
retry.targetedReteach: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g3-u05-l06-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step.
retry.supportedReattempt: Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g3-u05-l06-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check.
retry.feedback: Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments.
retry.parallelReattempt: Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g3-u05-l06-retry-pair without the coach prompt.

guardianInvolvement.role: Optional coach only; no guardian attestation is required.
guardianInvolvement.signOffBoundary: A guardian attestation certifies only that the named physical event occurred. It never scores the learner reflection or proves effort, honesty, maturity, responsibility, diagnosis, or character.

safety.stopRule: Stop the physical route when permission, supervision, a safe setting, or an expected material is missing, or when a new hazard appears. Continue only when the authorized adult resolves it; otherwise use the complete fictional route.
safety.physicalBoundary: The learner follows the source safety notes and never performs adult-only handling, transport, account, legal, medical, heat, sharp-tool, electrical, chemical, or machine actions.
safety.noShameRule: Describe only the observable step, condition, evidence, or revision. Never label the learner, household, body, ability, effort, maturity, responsibility, or character.

privacy.rule: Collect the smallest process record that shows the lesson steps. A learner may choose fictional details and may decline private disclosure without losing credit.
doNotCollect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations
account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details
photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules

may: coach the guided and retry cards
mayNot: observe or claim a physical condition
tutorBoundary.physicalCompletionRule: Tutor or AI may coach. Tutor or AI may not certify that a real-world physical action occurred.
tutorBoundary.missingResourceAction: Stop and name the unresolved resource. Do not fabricate it; use another complete delivered route only when every resource for that route resolves.
